items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: Carole King, Carly Simon, James Taylor, Elton John — you know the first thing I figured out how to play on the piano, a kind of a pop tune, was “Your Song” by Elton John.

ctx.x: Did the pop music you listened to as a kid have any influence on your writing?

It definitely did, and I’m still perfectly happy to just write a tune and, you know, in a style that may be more folk or folk-jazz influenced or whatever it might be. But yeah, Carole King, Carly Simon, James Taylor, Elton John — you know the first thing I figured out how to play on the piano, a kind of a pop tune, was “Your Song” by Elton John. And I loved the way he played, I loved his melodicism, and there’s some — I don’t want to say any of that music is simple. I mean it might not be as — you know there…
and there. But yeah, no I love that music and it’s still is big part I think of who I am as a musician.
